newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Konzum changes capital increase terms.
newsitem.headline: Konzum changes capital increase terms.

text.p: The shareholders of Hungarian trading and industrial company Konzum Rt modified the terms of an already approved capital increase on Monday at an extraordinary general meeting.

The modified conditions mandated Konzum's board to increase the current 860 million forints share capital by up to a nominal 826 million forints by the end of 1997, documents of the general meeting said.
The earlier terms called for a capital increase by June 30, 1997 and the nominal value of shares to be issued newly, was limited to 39 percent of the share capital, it said.

The capital increase can be implemented via the issue of new shares and via the conversion of Konzum's assets above its share capital into share capital, Konzum said as part of its amended articles of association.

Forlev Kft, the owner of Fordan, a Hungarian group of construction and fuel retail firms and diversified service companies, was mandated to buy the new shares, to be issued at the face value of 400 forints.
In January-June 1996 Konzum posted a pre-tax loss of 116.3 million forints on net sales of 597.2 million forints.

The Fordan group generated a consolidated profit of 22 million forints in this period on net sales of 1.13 billion forints. It was not immediately clear whether or not this is a pre-tax or an after-tax profit.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Konzum shares closed at 279 forints, up four.
